html:
The overthrow of Tarquin the Proud, seventh and last king of Rome, dated by Roman tradition to 509 BCE. It began the Roman Republic.

In the story told by Livy, the king's son raped Lucretia, a noblewoman, who then took her own life. Lucius Junius Brutus led the nobles in driving out the royal family. Rome replaced the king with two consuls elected each year, so no one man would hold power for long. Tarquin sought help from the Etruscan king Lars Porsena and the Latin towns, but failed to return.

Historians accept that Rome's kings, several of them Etruscan, fell around this time, though the details are legend. The Temple of Jupiter on the Capitol was dedicated in the first year of the Republic.

Romans hated the word "king" ever after. When Julius Caesar seemed to want the title, a later Brutus, who claimed descent from the first, helped kill him.
sum: The overthrow of Tarquin the Proud, seventh and last king of Rome, dated by Roman tradition to 509 BCE. It began the Roman Republic.
